Agent Name: Planner
Step Number: 0
Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a fundamental error in scientific reasoning and task interpretation by prioritizing a theoretical calculation (Archimedes' principle) over the practical necessity of physical testing. The core of the question asks for the "best way" to be *sure* the boats will float without tipping. In engineering and experimental science, calculations are estimates subject to material variability and construction imperfections, whereas constructing a prototype and testing it is the only definitive method to verify performance in the real world. The Planner incorrectly dismissed the need for a prototype (Option A) as "unnecessary," failing to recognize that for a hands-on student project involving variable materials and construction, empirical testing is the standard and most reliable solution. This aligns with the error pattern of "Misalignment with Ground Truth" and "Over-reliance on supplementary information" (theoretical principles) over the primary context (practical verification).
